verses.title: Ayat al-Kursi (The Throne Verse)
verses.textIndopak: اللهُ لَآ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَۚ اَلۡحَىُّ الۡقَيُّوۡمُۚ لَا تَاۡخُذُهٗ سِنَةٌ وَّلَا نَوۡمٌؕ لَهٗ مَا فِى السَّمٰوٰتِ وَمَا فِى الۡاَرۡضِؕ مَنۡ ذَا الَّذِىۡ يَشۡفَعُ عِنۡدَهٗۤ اِلَّا بِاِذۡنِهٖؕ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ اَيۡدِيۡهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۚ وَلَا يُحِيۡطُوۡنَ بِشَىۡءٍ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهٖۤ اِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضَۚ وَلَا يَـُٔوۡدُهٗ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ الۡعَلِىُّ الۡعَظِيۡمُ
verses.translation: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that could intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
verses.significance: Referred to by the Prophet ﷺ as the greatest verse in the entire Quran (Sayyidat Ayi al-Quran). It encompasses ten distinct statements celebrating divine oneness, absolute life, eternal self-sufficiency, limitless dominion, supreme knowledge, and effortless preservation of the cosmos.
verses.blessings: Reciting it after every obligatory prayer leaves only death between the believer and Paradise. Recited before sleep, an angelic guardian is appointed over you and no devil can approach you until morning.
verses.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 2311, Sahih Muslim 810, Sunan an-Nasa'i (Al-Kubra 9848)

verses.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opener)
verses.textIndopak: بِسۡمِ اللهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِ ۝١ اَلۡحَمۡدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ الۡعٰلَمِيۡنَۙ ۝٢ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِۙ ۝٣ مٰلِكِ يَوۡمِ الدِّيۡنِؕ ۝٤ اِيَّاكَ نَعۡبُدُ وَاِيَّاكَ نَسۡتَعِيۡنُؕ ۝٥ اِهۡدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الۡمُسۡتَقِيۡمَۙ ۝٦ صِرَاطَ الَّذِيۡنَ اَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غَيۡرِ الۡمَغۡضُوۡبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا الضَّآلِّيۡنَ ۝٧
verses.translation: In the name of Allāh, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. All praise is due to Allāh, Lord of the worlds - The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Sovereign of the Day of Recompense. It is You we worship and You we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path - The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
verses.significance: The Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab) and the Seven Oft-Repeated verses (As-Sab' al-Mathani). It establishes the fundamental paradigm of servanthood: sincere praise of Allah followed by the supreme request for divine guidance.
verses.blessings: An intimate dialogue where Allah responds to every verse recited. Also known as Ash-Shifa (The Cure), widely recited as Ruqyah for healing physical and spiritual ailments.

verses.title: Surah Al-Ikhlas (Purity of Faith)
verses.textIndopak: قُلۡ هُوَ اللهُ اَحَدٌۚ ۝١ اَللهُ الصَّمَدُۚ ۝٢ لَمۡ يَلِدۡ وَلَمۡ يُوۡلَدۡۙ ۝٣ وَلَمۡ يَكُنۡ لَّهٗ كُفُوًا اَحَدٌ ۝٤
verses.translation: Say, 'He is Allāh, [who is] One, Allāh, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent.'
verses.significance: The purest and most concise distillation of pure monotheism (Tawheed) in scripture, entirely dedicated to defining the absolute transcendence, uniqueness, and self-sufficiency of Allah (As-Samad).
verses.blessings: Equated by the Prophet ﷺ to one-third of the entire Quran in reward and meaning. Reciting it 3 times morning and evening with Al-Falaq and An-Nas provides complete spiritual protection.

verses.title: Surah Al-Falaq (The Daybreak / Protection)
verses.textIndopak: قُلۡ اَعُوۡذُ بِرَبِّ الۡفَلَقِۙ ۝١ مِنۡ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَۙ ۝٢ وَمِنۡ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ اِذَا وَقَبَۙ ۝٣ وَمِنۡ شَرِّ النَّفّٰثٰتِ فِى الۡعُقَدِۙ ۝٤ وَمِنۡ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ اِذَا حَسَدَ ۝٥
verses.translation: Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak From the evil of that which He created And from the evil of darkness when it settles And from the evil of the blowers in knots And from the evil of an envier when he envies.'
verses.significance: One of the two primary refuge-seeking Surahs (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn). It seeks divine sanctuary against external evils: the darkness of the night, occult witchcraft, and the venom of envious eyes (hasad).
verses.blessings: The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge using these two surahs above all others once they were revealed. Reciting them protects against the evil eye, jealousy, and dark spiritual harm.

verses.title: Surah An-Nas (Mankind / Spiritual Refuge)
verses.textIndopak: قُلۡ اَعُوۡذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِۙ ۝١ مَلِكِ النَّاسِۙ ۝٢ اِلٰهِ النَّاسِۙ ۝٣ مِنۡ شَرِّ الۡوَسۡوَاسِ ەۙ الۡخَـنَّاسِ۪ ۝٤ الَّذِىۡ يُوَسۡوِسُ فِىۡ صُدُوۡرِ النَّاسِۙ ۝٥ مِنَ الۡجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ ۝٦
verses.translation: Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, The Sovereign of mankind, The God of mankind, From the evil of the retreating whisperer - Who whispers into the breasts of mankind - From among the jinn and mankind.'
verses.significance: The closing chapter of the Quran, invoking Allah by His three majestic attributes (Lord, King, and God of mankind) to seek protection against internal and psychic whispers (waswas), anxiety, doubts, and hidden tempters.
verses.blessings: Provides immunity against obsessive doubts (waswas), paranoia, insomnia, and spiritual vulnerability.

verses.title: Amanar-Rasool (The Last Two Verses of Al-Baqarah)
verses.textIndopak: اٰمَنَ الرَّسُوۡلُ بِمَاۤ اُنۡزِلَ اِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ رَّبِّهٖ وَالۡمُؤۡمِنُوۡنَؕ كُلٌّ اٰمَنَ بِاللهِ وَمَلٰٓئِكَتِهٖ وَكُتُبِهٖ وَرُسُلِهٖ۫ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ اَحَدٍ مِّنۡ رُّسُلِهٖؕ وَقَالُوۡا سَمِعۡنَا وَاَطَعۡنَا غُفۡرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَاِلَيۡكَ الۡمَصِيۡرُ ۝٢٨٥ لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفۡسًا اِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاؕ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا اكۡتَسَبَتۡؕ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَاۤ اِنۡ نَّسِيۡنَاۤ اَوۡ اَخۡطَاۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَاۤ اِصۡرًا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهٗ عَلَى الَّذِيۡنَ مِنۡ قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهٖۚ وَاعۡفُ عَنَّاٝ وَاغۡفِرۡ لَنَاٝ وَارۡحَمۡنَاٝ اَنۡتَ مَوۡلٰىنَا فَانۡصُرۡنَا عَلَى الۡقَوۡمِ الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ ۝٢٨٦
verses.translation: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allāh and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers.' And they say, 'We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.' Allāh does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. 'Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.'
verses.significance: Gifted directly to the Prophet ﷺ during the Night Journey (Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj) from beneath the Divine Throne. It seals the Quran's longest surah with an absolute surrender of faith and an all-encompassing prayer for forgiveness and relief from overwhelming burdens.
verses.blessings: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him' (protecting him from harm, evil, and serving as sufficient devotion).

verses.title: Verse of Patience and Prayer
verses.textIndopak: يٰٓاَيُّهَا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوا اسۡتَعِيۡنُوۡا بِالصَّبۡرِ وَالصَّلٰوةِؕ اِنَّ اللهَ مَعَ الصّٰبِرِيۡنَ
verses.translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allāh is with the patient.
verses.significance: A foundational divine commandment prescribing the two ultimate spiritual anchors in times of crisis: internal steadfastness (Sabr) and outward communion with God through prayer (Salah), backed by the promise of Allah's special companionship (Ma'iyyah).
verses.blessings: Whenever a matter distressed the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, he would immediately hasten to stand in prayer, finding serenity and divine assistance.
verses.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1319, Tafsir Ibn Kathir

verses.title: Verse of Boundless Divine Mercy
verses.textIndopak: قُلۡ يٰعِبَادِىَ الَّذِيۡنَ اَسۡرَفُوۡا عَلٰٓى اَنۡفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُوۡا مِنۡ رَّحۡمَةِ اللهِؕ اِنَّ اللهَ يَغۡفِرُ الذُّنُوۡبَ جَمِيۡعًاؕ اِنَّهٗ هُوَ الۡغَفُوۡرُ الرَّحِيۡمُ
verses.translation: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
verses.significance: Considered by scholars like Abdullah ibn Abbas to be the most hopeful verse in the entire Quran. Allah affectionately calls the sinners 'My servants' (ya 'ibadiya), forbidding despair and confirming that sincere repentance obliterates every sin without exception.
verses.blessings: Reignites hope in the heart of the repentant believer, dispelling despair and confirming that God's mercy encompasses all human frailties.

verses.title: Dua of Prophet Yunus (In the Belly of the Whale)
verses.textIndopak: لَّآ اِلٰهَ اِلَّآ اَنۡتَ سُبۡحٰنَكَۖ اِنِّىۡ كُنۡتُ مِنَ الظّٰلِمِيۡنَ
verses.translation: There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.
verses.significance: The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Prophet Yunus) when trapped in the triple darkness of the night, the deep sea, and the whale's belly. It combines pure monotheism, sanctification of Allah from flaw, and humble confession of fault.
verses.blessings: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'No Muslim suppliant ever calls upon Allah with this supplication for any matter, except that Allah answers him.'

verses.title: The Comprehensive Dua (Rabbana Atina)
verses.textIndopak: رَبَّنَاۤ اٰتِنَا فِى الدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةً وَّفِى الۡاٰخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَّقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
verses.translation: Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
verses.significance: The most frequent and beloved supplication of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It brings total equilibrium to a believer's aspirations by asking for all worldly blessings (faith, health, sustenance, peace) and the supreme blessings of the Hereafter (Paradise and salvation from Hell).
verses.blessings: Anas ibn Malik reported that this was the single most common supplication made by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in all circumstances.

verses.title: Dua of Prophet Musa for Ease & Speech
verses.textIndopak: رَبِّ اشۡرَحۡ لِىۡ صَدۡرِىۙ ۝٢٥ وَيَسِّرۡ لِىۡۤ اَمۡرِىۙ ۝٢٦ وَاحۡلُلۡ عُقۡدَةً مِّنۡ لِّسَانِىۙ ۝٢٧ يَفۡقَهُوۡا قَوۡلِى۪ ۝٢٨
verses.translation: My Lord, expand for me my chest [with assurance], And ease for me my task, And untie the knot from my tongue, That they may understand my speech.
verses.significance: Prophet Musa's prayer before confronting the tyrant Pharaoh. It seeks spiritual confidence (expansion of the heart), divine facilitation of difficult missions, and clarity of articulation.
verses.blessings: A renowned spiritual remedy for overcoming anxiety, speech hesitation, nervousness, and challenging examinations or presentations.

verses.title: Dua of Prophet Musa in Extreme Need
verses.textIndopak: رَبِّ اِنِّىۡ لِمَاۤ اَنۡزَلۡتَ اِلَىَّ مِنۡ خَيۡرٍ فَقِيۡرٌ
verses.translation: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.
verses.significance: Uttered by Prophet Musa as an exhausted, homeless refugee under the shade in Madyan. Within hours of this sincere prayer, Allah granted him honorable employment, a righteous family, marriage, and divine protection.
verses.blessings: Widely recited by believers seeking lawful sustenance, employment, marriage, and relief from poverty and destitution.

verses.title: Dua of Prophet Ayyub for Healing
verses.textIndopak: اَنِّىۡ مَسَّنِىَ الضُّرُّ وَاَنۡتَ اَرۡحَمُ الرّٰحِمِيۡنَ
verses.translation: Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
verses.significance: Prophet Ayyub's dignified, gentle plea after enduring years of devastating illness, loss of children, and loss of wealth. He describes adversity with humility without complaining against his Lord.
verses.blessings: Immediately following this prayer, Allah commanded him to strike the earth, curing his illness completely and returning double what he had lost.

verses.title: Dua for Steadfastness of the Heart (Rabbana La Tuzigh)
verses.textIndopak: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغۡ قُلُوۡبَنَا بَعۡدَ اِذۡ هَدَيۡتَنَا وَهَبۡ لَنَا مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ رَحۡمَةًۚ اِنَّكَ اَنۡتَ الۡوَهَّابُ
verses.translation: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
verses.significance: A plea made by those firmly grounded in knowledge (Ar-Rasikhuna fil-'Ilm), acknowledging that steadfastness upon truth is a divine gift that must be continuously guarded.
verses.blessings: Protects against spiritual regression, hypocrisy, ideological deviation, and hardness of heart.

verses.title: Dua of Adam and Hawwa for Repentance
verses.textIndopak: رَبَّنَا ظَلَمۡنَاۤ اَنۡفُسَنَا وَاِنۡ لَّمۡ تَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَتَرۡحَمۡنَا لَنَكُوۡنَنَّ مِنَ الۡخٰسِرِيۡنَ
verses.translation: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.
verses.significance: The words of repentance taught by Allah directly to Adam (Al-Baqarah 2:37) to restore him to divine favor after his slip in Paradise. The archetypal prayer of human repentance.
verses.blessings: Allah accepted Adam's repentance through these blessed words, demonstrating that sincere admission of fault with plea for mercy guarantees divine acceptance.

verses.title: Dua for Righteous Family and Children
verses.textIndopak: رَبَّنَا هَبۡ لَنَا مِنۡ اَزۡوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ اَعۡيُنٍ وَّاجۡعَلۡنَا لِلۡمُتَّقِيۡنَ اِمَامًا
verses.translation: Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous.
verses.significance: The defining prayer of the Servants of the Most Merciful ('Ibadur-Rahman). 'Comfort to the eyes' (Qurrata A'yun) signifies pure joy, peace, and delight in seeing loved ones obedient to God.
verses.blessings: Fosters love, harmony, religious commitment, and righteous uprightness within marriages and family lineages.

verses.title: Dua for Parents (Mercy in Old Age)
verses.textIndopak: رَّبِّ ارۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيٰنِىۡ صَغِيۡرًا
verses.translation: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.
verses.significance: Directly mandated by Allah in the Quran as an eternal obligation of filial piety (Birr al-Walidayn). It connects present supplication with the vulnerability and selfless tenderness of childhood nurturing.
verses.blessings: Elevates the ranks of parents in Paradise even after their death, as confirmed in the authentic Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ.

verses.title: Dua for Increase in Knowledge (Rabbi Zidni 'Ilma)
verses.textIndopak: فَتَعٰلَى اللهُ الۡمَلِكُ الۡحَقُّۚ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِالۡقُرۡاٰنِ مِنۡ قَبۡلِ اَنۡ يُّقۡضٰٓى اِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهٗۖ وَقُلْ رَّبِّ زِدۡنِىۡ عِلۡمًا
verses.translation: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'
verses.significance: The only matter in the entire Quran where Allah commanded His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to pray for an increase (Ziyadah) was knowledge ('Ilm).
verses.blessings: Opens the intellect, sharpens retention, and blesses beneficial spiritual and worldly knowledge.

verses.title: Hasbunallah (Sufficiency of Allah)
verses.textIndopak: حَسۡبُنَا اللهُ وَنِعۡمَ الۡوَكِيۡلُ
verses.translation: Sufficient for us is Allāh, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs.
verses.significance: Recited by Prophet Ibrahim when cast into the roaring fire, and recited by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions when faced with an overwhelming hostile army after the battle of Uhud.
verses.blessings: Turns fear into divine security, victory, and unwavering serenity. Allah followed it with: 'So they returned with grace and bounty from Allah, untouched by harm.'

verses.title: Ayat an-Nur (The Verse of Light)
verses.textIndopak: اللهُ نُوۡرُ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِؕ مَثَلُ نُوۡرِهٖ كَمِشۡكٰوةٍ فِيۡهَا مِصۡبَاحٌؕ اَلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِىۡ زُجَاجَةٍؕ اَلزُّجَاجَةُ كَاَنَّهَا كَوۡكَبٌ دُرِّىٌّ يُّوۡقَدُ مِنۡ شَجَرَةٍ مُّبٰرَكَةٍ زَيۡتُوۡنَةٍ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةٍ وَّلَا غَرۡبِيَّةٍۙ يَّكَادُ زَيۡتُهَا يُضِىۡٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارٌؕ نُوۡرٌ عَلٰى نُوۡرٍؕ يَهۡدِى اللهُ لِنُوۡرِهٖ مَنۡ يَّشَآءُؕ وَيَضۡرِبُ اللهُ الۡاَمۡثَالَ لِلنَّاسِؕ وَاللهُ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيۡمٌ
verses.translation: Allāh is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allāh guides to His light whom He wills. And Allāh presents examples for the people, and Allāh is Knowing of all things.
verses.significance: One of the most mystical and profound parables in scripture. It describes the divine illumination that enlightens the cosmos and the pristine, luminous faith glowing within the believer's purified heart.
verses.blessings: Inspires profound spiritual insight, clarity of intuition, and internal peace amidst worldly darkness.
verses.reference: Surah An-Nur (24:35), Mishkat al-Anwar by Al-Ghazali

verses.title: Ease with Hardship (Ash-Sharh)
verses.textIndopak: فَاِنَّ مَعَ الۡعُسۡرِ يُسۡرًاۙ ۝٥ اِنَّ مَعَ الۡعُسۡرِ يُسۡرًاؕ ۝٦
verses.translation: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
verses.significance: A repeated divine guarantee that hardship is never alone; ease is packaged right alongside it. In Arabic grammar, the hardship (Al-'Usr) is definite while ease (Yusr) is indefinite, leading scholars to declare: 'One hardship cannot overcome two eases.'
verses.blessings: Instills immediate optimism and patience, reminding the believer that relief is already unfolding simultaneously with trial.

verses.title: Dua of Zakariyya for Offspring
verses.textIndopak: رَبِّ هَبۡ لِىۡ مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةًۚ اِنَّكَ سَمِيۡعُ الدُّعَآءِ
verses.translation: My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.
verses.significance: Prophet Zakariyya's prayer in extreme old age when his wife was barren, inspired by witnessing Maryam's out-of-season fruits from Allah. It resulted in the miraculous birth of Prophet Yahya (John the Baptist).
verses.blessings: A powerful supplication for couples desiring righteous children and overcoming biological or worldly impediments through divine mercy.

verses.title: Dua of Ibrahim for Establishing Prayer
verses.textIndopak: رَبِّ اجۡعَلۡنِىۡ مُقِيۡمَ الصَّلٰوةِ وَمِنۡ ذُرِّيَّتِىۡۖ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلۡ دُعَآءِ ۝٤٠ رَبَّنَا اغۡفِرۡ لِىۡ وَلِوَالِدَىَّ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِيۡنَ يَوۡمَ يَقُوۡمُ الۡحِسَابُ ۝٤١
verses.translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established.
verses.significance: Prophet Ibrahim's prayer for spiritual steadfastness, generational devotion to Salah, and comprehensive forgiveness for oneself, one's parents, and the entire body of believers.
verses.blessings: Safeguards oneself and future generations from abandoning prayer, and earns forgiveness by interceding for all believing men and women.

verses.title: Closing Verses of Surah Al-Hashr (Divine Names)
verses.textIndopak: هُوَ اللهُ الَّذِىۡ لَآ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَۚ عَالِمُ الۡغَيۡبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِۚ هُوَ الرَّحۡمٰنُ الرَّحِيۡمُ ۝٢٢ هُوَ اللهُ الَّذِىۡ لَآ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَۚ اَلۡمَلِكُ الۡقُدُّوۡسُ السَّلٰمُ الۡمُؤۡمِنُ الۡمُهَيۡمِنُ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡجَبَّارُ الۡمُتَكَبِّرُؕ سُبۡحٰنَ اللهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُوۡنَ ۝٢٣ هُوَ اللهُ الۡخَالِقُ الۡبَارِئُ الۡمُصَوِّرُ لَهُ الۡاَسۡمَآءُ الۡحُسۡنٰىؕ يُسَبِّحُ لَهٗ مَا فِى السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِۚ وَهُوَ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡحَكِيۡمُ ۝٢٤
verses.translation: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him. He is Allāh, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
verses.significance: A breathtaking constellation of over 15 of Allah's Most Beautiful Names (Asma' Allah al-Husna), detailing His knowledge, supreme authority, transcendent holiness, creation, and majesty.
verses.blessings: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned that whoever recites these verses in the morning or evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him and if he dies that day, he dies as a martyr.
